Zurich Instruments Ltd. is a Swiss test and measurement company based in Zurich's Technopark. Founded in 2008 as a spin-off from ETH Zurich, it specializes in advanced scientific instrumentation for dynamic signal analysis. The company offers a range of high-performance instruments controlled via its LabOne software platform. Zurich Instruments is known for its innovative approach, utilizing FPGA-based digital signal processing to create compact, multifunctional tools. With a global presence, the company supports scientific research organizations and leading institutes, emphasizing ongoing innovation in sensitivity, speed, and accuracy.

With a team of over 100 employees, Pexapark is dedicated to digitizing the route to market for renewables, making it easier for energy players to execute deals and manage risks effectively.

The company is committed to quality, holding ISO 9001:2015 and ISO/IEC 17025:2017 certifications.

Biosynth is a life sciences company that specializes in reagents, custom synthesis, and manufacturing services. Founded in 1966, it has grown into a global provider of chemical and biochemical products through strategic mergers and acquisitions. Notably, the company merged with Carbosynth in 2019, enhancing its capabilities in carbohydrates, nucleosides, and enzyme substrates. In recent years, Biosynth has expanded its offerings by acquiring Vivitide, Pepscan, Aalto Bio Reagents, and EUCODIS Bioscience, further strengthening its position in peptide manufacturing and biological products.

Biosynth manufactures a wide range of products, including carbohydrates, nucleosides, peptides, antibodies, enzymes, and life sciences reagents. The company is known for its ability to deliver complex chemistry and biological raw materials. It also provides custom synthesis and manufacturing services, focusing on peptide synthesis, antibody production, and enzyme development. With facilities across three continents, Biosynth supports various sectors, including pharmaceuticals, life sciences, diagnostics, food, agrochemistry, and cosmetics, ensuring high-quality supply chains for its global clients.

Speedgoat caters to industries such as automotive, aerospace, industrial automation, power electronics, and green energy. The company emphasizes innovation and continuous learning, positioning itself as a leader in modular hardware for real-time testing. With a dedicated team of 51-200 employees, Speedgoat focuses on reducing development risks and enabling rapid iteration for its customers.

Debiopharm is a Swiss biopharmaceutical company founded in 1979, focused on innovation in oncology and infectious disease therapies. Headquartered in Lausanne, it operates through three entities: Debiopharm International, Debiopharm Research & Manufacturing, and another Debiopharm Research & Manufacturing. The company aims to develop tomorrow's standard of care and enhance patient quality of life.

Debiopharm specializes in rescuing promising compounds and in-licensing high-potential molecules from universities and biotech firms. It finances clinical development up to Phase II and partners with large pharmaceutical companies for global commercialization. Notable marketed products include triptorelin, a sustained-release GnRH agonist, and oxaliplatin, a chemotherapy agent. The company has 15 ongoing drug programs targeting novel mechanisms in cancer and infections, with a focus on innovative therapies addressing high unmet needs. Debiopharm actively seeks partnerships to advance its pipeline and improve patient access to its therapies.

The company serves a global market, with a strong presence in Europe, South America, and Africa, providing solutions to major rail operators and energy-intensive industries.

The company also offers contract manufacturing services for active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and finished products. With a commitment to quality and sustainability, Helsinn adheres to current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) standards and has established a presence in about 150 countries through direct operations and partnerships.

Synhelion is a Swiss cleantech company founded in 2016, focusing on producing renewable synthetic solar fuels to decarbonize transportation. The company utilizes concentrated solar heat to create fuels, aiming to replace fossil fuels with drop-in solar fuels that are compatible with existing infrastructure. Headquartered in Lugano, Synhelion operates with around 29 employees and emphasizes high-temperature solar process heat for various industries, including cement manufacturing.

The company has achieved significant milestones, such as producing the world's first carbon-neutral fuel from air and sunlight in 2019 and inaugurating the DAWN plant in Jülich, Germany, in 2024, which is the first industrial-scale solar fuel facility. Synhelion's products include Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), solar diesel, and synthetic crude oil, all designed to support defossilization across multiple transport sectors. The company collaborates with major partners like SWISS and Lufthansa Group to scale its solar kerosene and has demonstrated its fuels in various vehicles, including cars and motorcycles.

Santhera Pharmaceuticals is a Swiss specialty pharmaceutical company founded in 2004 and based in Pratteln, Switzerland. The company focuses on developing and commercializing innovative medicines for rare neuromuscular and pulmonary diseases, addressing significant unmet medical needs in Europe, North America, and Asia. With a commitment to improving patients' quality of life, Santhera emphasizes treatments for conditions like Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD).

The company's lead candidate, Vamorolone, is a dissociative steroid currently under review by regulatory authorities, including the FDA and EMA, for the treatment of DMD. Additionally, Santhera is advancing Lonodelestat, which is in Phase 2a studies for cystic fibrosis and other acute pulmonary conditions. The company is positioned to explore partnerships for further development and licensing of its promising therapies.

Stratpharma AG is a Swiss medical devices and pharmaceutical company founded in 2005 and based in Basel. The company specializes in innovative film-forming gel products designed for various applications, including dermatology, wound care, plastic surgery, and oncology. Led by CEO Darren Kerr, Stratpharma is committed to delivering high-quality medical solutions that enhance patient outcomes. Its products are available in over 50 countries, with a strong presence in Central and Eastern Europe, Asia, and other regions.

Stratpharma develops and commercializes medical devices, particularly film-forming gels that serve as flexible wound dressings. These gels are used in cosmetic dermatology, scar management, and post-procedure care, among other areas. The company offers five key products, including Strataderm, a leading scar management solution in China, and Stratamark for stretchmarks. Stratpharma focuses on meeting the diverse needs of healthcare professionals, patients, and institutions, ensuring accessibility to its innovative solutions worldwide.

Casale SA, also known as Casale Group, is a Swiss engineering company based in Lugano, specializing in integrated technologies and solutions for the chemical and fertilizer industries. Founded in 1921 by Luigi Casale, the company has over 100 years of experience and employs more than 400 professionals across various global locations, including the Czech Republic, China, Brazil, India, and the United States.

Casale offers a wide range of services, including engineering, contracting, and construction for new plants and plant revamping. Their expertise covers the entire project lifecycle, from feasibility studies to long-term maintenance. The company provides know-how and licensing for chemical synthesis technologies, engineering services, equipment supply, and sustainable solutions aimed at enhancing efficiency and reducing carbon footprints. Casale is committed to innovation for sustainability, focusing on greener technologies and processes, including the production of fertilizers and base chemicals, as well as sustainable innovations like blue hydrogen and CO₂ utilization.

Actelion, now part of Janssen Pulmonary Hypertension under Johnson & Johnson, is a Swiss biopharmaceutical company dedicated to developing treatments for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and other rare diseases. Founded in 1997, Actelion has built a strong legacy in addressing rare and orphan diseases, particularly PAH, which is a serious condition characterized by high blood pressure in the lungs.

The company offers a range of therapies for PAH, including oral, inhaled, and intravenous options. Notable products include Tracleer, the first oral endothelin receptor antagonist approved for PAH, and Opsumit, another effective treatment in this category. Actelion also provides therapies for conditions such as Type 1 Gaucher disease and systemic sclerosis. Janssen continues to invest in research and development to enhance patient outcomes and support, aiming to make PAH a manageable condition through innovative treatments and partnerships with healthcare systems.

It serves pharmaceutical partners globally, focusing on drug development in areas like oncology and respiratory medicine, while also maintaining its own product pipeline.

Novartis Global Health is a division of Novartis, a leading pharmaceutical company based in Switzerland. This unit is dedicated to improving health outcomes for lower-income populations by delivering medicines and healthcare solutions for diseases that have seen limited investment in research and development. Novartis Global Health aims to address significant global health challenges through an integrated approach to disease management.

The division focuses on four main programs targeting malaria, sickle cell disease, Chagas disease, and leprosy. Additionally, it addresses other critical health issues such as avoidable blindness and antimicrobial resistance. Novartis's research operations, including specialized institutes, support these efforts by developing treatments for diseases prevalent in the developing world. The division emphasizes affordability, adaptive drug development, and strengthening healthcare systems to enhance access to its solutions.
